reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. render-b.js:416 builds h("input.b-input", { id: "b-edit-title", type: "text", value: record.title }) with no on: block, and the only "done" handler (render-b.js:511) is closeEditor — nothing reads the field, ever. Driven at ?v=approach&state=owner-editing: filled #b-edit-title with "Send the invitations to everyone"; the row title stayed "Send the invitations" while the panel was still open and after Done, and .b-grab's aria-label stayed "Send the invitations, Saturday 8 August, in 23 days. Shown to guests. Open to change it." No message says the edit was dropped. This is the first field of the panel the whole owner story opens with, and every other control beside it (the four steppers, the Shown/Hidden segment, Delete) writes live, so the dead one is indistinguishable from the live ones. The second half is also true: "Add a moment" (render-b.js:559, handler 515-518) calls openEditor on root.querySelector(".b-item") — driven from owner-flight, 7 rows before the press and 7 after, and the panel opens pre-filled with the existing first row's "Menu tasting at The Orchard". A create verb that creates nothing, over a title field that cannot be written, leaves this direction with no path by which an owner puts a new moment on the plan. Neither gate covers it: interaction-check.mjs touches #b-edit-title exactly once (line 462) and only to prove Ctrl+Z stays out of the way inside a text field; it never asserts the field persists. No constraint is touched — no colour, no weight, no architecture.
sharpenedFix: The writer is right; three corrections before it lands. (1) Route through data-full, not textContent alone — core clamp() (render-core.js:200) reads data-full first and rewrites textContent from it, so setting only textContent is erased by the next settle. Set data-full = v, then textContent = v, then re-label the grab exactly as setVisibility does: grab.setAttribute("aria-label", grabLabel(record, item.getAttribute("data-date"), Number(item.getAttribute("data-away")), item.getAttribute("data-visibility") === "hidden")). (2) Do not call C.settle() on every keystroke — settle() re-clamps every [data-clamp] node in the document and then re-place()s every .b-measure, which is a full re-layout per character while the field also holds focus. Write the text on input, and debounce the settle to a frame (requestAnimationFrame, cancelling the pending one) or defer it to change/blur/Done. (3) Drop the `if (!v) return` swallow: an owner who selects-all and retypes passes through empty and would otherwise leave the row showing a title the field no longer contains. Write record.title = v on every input and let the row fall back to a stated placeholder when v is empty rather than silently keeping the old string. Also note the deliberate asymmetry: record is the live F.milestones object (recordFor, render-b.js:86), so a title written here survives a re-mount into Preview/Publish/print, while setAway's date changes are DOM-only and do not — that is the better behaviour, not a bug, but it is worth choosing on purpose. For the bar: a real add cannot be DOM-only. editor() and setAway() both resolve their record through recordFor(id) against F.milestones, so appending a row with a fresh id and no fixture record makes record undefined and editor() throws on record.title. A real add must push { id, title: "New moment", date: F.plusDays(clock, 1) } into F.milestones first, then build the row, then place(), then openEditor and focus #b-edit-title — and insert the row at the head of .b-measure rather than appending it, since the list is announced "nearest first" and place() only sorts geometry, not DOM order. If that is more than this round wants, the inert("Adding comes next") substitution at render-b.js:559 is the honest alternative and should be taken instead — but the title field must be fixed either way.
